(Fetched via WebFetch text extraction — condensed by fetch tool; direct curl blocked. Times of Israel newsroom. By Emanuel Fabian and ToI Staff, October 17, 2026, 6:12 pm Israel time)
European diplomatic vehicles were targeted by Israeli settlers in the West Bank village of Taybeh on Saturday during a visit to observe the olive harvest. According to video evidence, a diplomatic vehicle had its window smashed by stone-throwing attackers.

The IDF stated it "strongly condemns the severe act of violence" while noting the diplomatic delegation "did not coordinate" their visit with the military. Police launched an investigation and the Foreign Ministry worked to identify victims and suspects.

In separate incidents throughout the day, approximately three Palestinians sustained injuries in various settler attacks. Settlers reportedly killed around 20 Palestinian-owned sheep during a raid on a farm in Kafr Malik.

Additional violence occurred in Deir Jarir village, where settlers allegedly fired live ammunition at Palestinians harvesting olives, eventually forcing them to leave their agricultural land. The Palestinian news agency claimed settlers operated under IDF protection, though the military did not immediately respond to inquiries.

Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine underwent surgery Saturday following an October 16 beating by settlers. She sustained severe injuries including a cut finger, broken rib, and multiple fractured vertebrae while attempting to photograph the olive harvest.

The European Council urged Israel to "immediately reverse the expansion of settlements" and warned against bidding on E1 settlement construction contracts, calling settlements "illegal under international law."
